title: Audit Findings Summary

text: Executive Summary This confidential report synthesizes observations from internal compliance assessments and external regulatory inspections completed during the fiscal year across Novacure Labs facilities. Dr. Meera Iyer, QA Head, issued this summary for management review.

text: Data Integrity Policy Document ID: DI-001 | Version: v1.2 | Date: 2025-02-14 | Author: Dr. Meera Iyer | Owner: Dr. Meera Iyer
title: Data Integrity Policy
author: Dr. Meera Iyer

text: 1. Policy Statement Novacure Labs strictly enforces data integrity principles across all computerized systems, laboratory instrumentation, paper records, and data archives. Truthful, contemporaneous, and uncompromised data is the core of our license to operate.
title: Data Integrity Policy
author: Dr. Meera Iyer

text: 2. ALCOA+ Principles All GxP data generated must be Attributable, Legible, Contemporaneous, Original, and Accurate. In addition, data must remain Complete, Consistent, Enduring, and Available throughout the record retention period.
title: Data Integrity Policy
author: Dr. Meera Iyer

text: 3. Electronic System Controls Computerized systems must feature role-based permissions, unique user credentials, and active automated audit trails. Shared generic passwords are categorically prohibited. Audit trail reviews must be executed prior to batch release.
title: Data Integrity Policy
author: Dr. Meera Iyer

text: 4. Enforcement and Governance Authored and authorized by Dr. Meera Iyer, QA Head. Any deliberate manipulation, backdating, deletion, or omission of GxP data constitutes gross misconduct and grounds for immediate dismissal and regulatory notification.
title: Data Integrity Policy
author: Dr. Meera Iyer

title: Quality Manual
author: Dr. Meera Iyer

text: 1. Corporate Quality Commitment Novacure Labs is dedicated to maintaining the highest standards of cGMP compliance, patient safety, and operational excellence across pharmaceutical manufacturing and testing operations.
title: Quality Manual
author: Dr. Meera Iyer

text: 2. Quality Governance Framework The Quality Assurance organization operates independently from production. Dr. Meera Iyer, QA Head, directs the executive quality committee. Priya Rao, QA Lead, owns deviation management and ensures operational compliance across all processing lines.
title: Quality Manual
author: Dr. Meera Iyer

text: 3. Deviation and Risk Management Quality risk management principles (ICH Q9) govern all deviation investigations, change controls, and CAPA systems. All operational personnel are required to flag potential compliance risks without delay.
title: Quality Manual
author: Dr. Meera Iyer

text: 4. Document Control Hierarchy The documentation pyramid consists of Level 1 Quality Manual, Level 2 Corporate Policies, Level 3 Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Level 4 Work Instructions, and Level 5 Batch Records and Forms.

text: SOP-001 Deviation Handling Document ID: SOP-001 | Version: v1.0 | Effective Date: 2025-01-15 | Author: Priya Rao 1. Purpose This Standard Operating Procedure establishes the mandatory process for identifying, documenting, triaging, and investigating deviations occurring during GMP manufacturing, packaging, testing, and storage operations at Novacure Labs. 2. Scope This procedure applies to all operational personnel, quality control analysts, warehouse operators, and validation engineers across all commercial and clinical production facilities at Novacure Labs. 3. Responsibilities Priya Rao, QA Lead, owns deviation management. The QA Lead is responsible for deviation classification, root-cause investigation approvals, and corrective action assignment. Department heads must ensure immediate reporting. 4. Procedure - Notification and Reporting Every deviation must be reported to QA within 24 hours of discovery. The reporting associate must execute immediate containment to prevent non-conforming product distribution and initiate an electronic deviation record in the QMS. 5. Procedure - Investigation and Root Cause For
title: SOP-001 Deviation Handling
author: Priya Rao

text: non-conforming product distribution and initiate an electronic deviation record in the QMS. 5. Procedure - Investigation and Root Cause For critical and major deviations, a formal root-cause analysis must be conducted using Ishikawa fishbone diagrams or 5-Why methodology. The investigation must be completed and submitted for QA review within 30 calendar days. 6. Batch Disposition and Record Retention Batches implicated in open deviations cannot be released for commercial distribution until all root-cause evaluations are concluded and signed off by Quality Assurance leadership. All records must be retained for at least 10 years.
title: SOP-001 Deviation Handling
author: Priya Rao

text: SOP-014 Cold-Chain Storage v2 Document ID: SOP-014-v2 | Version: v2.0 | Effective Date: 2024-11-05 | Author: Arjun Menon 1. Purpose This procedure specifies storage conditions, cold-chain handling, and temperature monitoring standards for refrigerated pharmaceutical stock and bulk biological intermediates at Novacure Labs. 2. Scope and Specifications Vaccine batches must be stored at 2 to 8 °C. Applies to primary cold storage warehouse chambers and inter-facility cold-chain transfers. Temperature must be checked and recorded manually twice daily. 3. Temperature Excursion Management Temperature excursions of up to 12 hours do not require a deviation report. If an excursion exceeds 12 hours or rises above 12 °C, warehouse supervisors must notify the facility operations team. 4. Handling and Packaging Cold boxes must be packed using certified gel packs conditioning between -2 °C and 0 °C prior to batch loading. Shipments must not exceed 48 hours transit duration without ice replenishment. 5. Author and

text: SOP-014 Cold-Chain Storage v3 Document ID: SOP-014-v3 | Version: v3.0 | Effective Date: 2025-06-20 | Author: Arjun Menon 1. Purpose This standard operating procedure sets mandatory storage limits, continuous telemetric monitoring, and quarantine rules for all temperature-sensitive vaccine products at Novacure Labs, superseding SOP-014-v2. 2. Cold-Chain Specifications Vaccine batches must be stored at 2 to 8 °C. Storage units must maintain calibrated NIST-traceable multi-point temperature sensors with real-time electronic alerting enabled 24/7. 3. Excursion Response Protocol Any temperature excursion longer than 4 hours requires a deviation report. Upon detecting a temperature excursion exceeding validated boundaries for more than 4 hours, stock must be segregated into quarantine immediately. 4. Quarantine and QA Escalation Physical quarantine cages and electronic warehouse holds must be applied instantly. The Cold-Chain Supervisor and QA Lead must initiate a deviation report within 24 hours pursuant to SOP-001. 5. Responsibilities and Author Control Authored by Arjun Menon, Cold-Chain
title: SOP-014 Cold-Chain Storage v3
author: Arjun Menon

text: SOP-021 CAPA Management Document ID: SOP-021 | Version: v1.0 | Effective Date: 2025-03-10 | Author: Priya Rao 1. Purpose This procedure defines the requirements for initiating, evaluating, executing, and tracking Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPA) at Novacure Labs. 2. Scope Encompasses quality issues resulting from confirmed OOS analytical findings, repeated deviations, internal audit findings, and regulatory audit observations. 3. Responsibilities Priya Rao, QA Lead, owns deviation management and provides oversight for CAPA system governance. Dr. Meera Iyer, QA Head, holds final approval authority for CAPA closure. 4. Timelines and Investigation A CAPA must be raised and the investigation completed within 15 working days of an OOS result being confirmed. The root-cause investigation must document verifiable containment and systemic remediation actions. 5. Effectiveness Review Each CAPA action plan must specify an effectiveness verification milestone typically scheduled 60 to 90 days post-implementation to guarantee defect recurrence is eliminated.
title: SOP-021 CAPA Management
author: Priya Rao

text: Cold Storage Unit Equipment Manual Document ID: EQP-001 | Version: v1.0 | Effective Date: 2024-09-01 | Author: Vikram Shah 1. Equipment Identification and Architecture This manual governs industrial refrigeration units Unit-CR-01 and Unit-CR-02 manufactured for Novacure Labs. Authored by Vikram Shah, Production Manager, with maintenance schedules validated by Arjun Menon. 2. Temperature Control Loop and Tuning The refrigeration system is engineered to maintain target storage at 2 to 8 °C using redundant dual-stage scroll compressors and variable speed fan coils. Temperature feedback is captured via calibrated Pt100 RTD sensors. 3. Preventive Maintenance Routines Monthly maintenance includes inspection of evaporator coils, compressor oil levels, door gasket seals, and validation of automatic generator backup switchover circuits. 4. Emergency Response and Failsafe Modes In the event of compressor malfunction, secondary refrigeration circuits engage automatically within 60 seconds. Alarm sirens and SMS alerts trigger if compartment temperatures drift outside validated boundaries.
title: Cold Storage Unit Equipment Manual
author: Vikram Shah

text: Regulatory Guideline Summary Document ID: REG-001 | Version: v1.0 | Effective Date: 2025-05-12 | Author: Kavya Nair 1. Overview of Global Regulatory Expectations Regulatory health authorities including the FDA (21 CFR Part 11) and EMA (Annex 11) emphasize complete and verifiable traceability for all data used to demonstrate pharmaceutical safety, quality, and efficacy. Kavya Nair, Regulatory Affairs Manager, compiled this summary to support site compliance. 2. Statutory Audit Trail Obligations Audit trails must remain operational at all times without administrative bypass. Computer systems must log who created, modified, or deleted records, along with exact UTC timestamps and documented reasons for change. 3. Storage and Cold-Chain Validation Regulatory authorities require validated temperature mapping and monitoring systems. Temperature boundaries must be supported by stability profiles. Temperature controlled materials must be stored within validated limits such as 2 to 8 °C for refrigerated biological inventory. 4. text: Stability Study Report Document ID: STB-001 | Version: v1.0 | Effective Date: 2025-10-30 | Author: Dr. Meera Iyer 1. Study Objective and Experimental Design This stability report summarizes long-term and accelerated stability testing for commercial vaccine product lots manufactured at Novacure Labs. Dr. Meera Iyer, QA Head, supervised the study and approved the stability protocol. 2. Storage Conditions and Assay Results Long-term stability lots were maintained at 2 to 8 °C in qualified walk-in cold chambers over a 36-month monitoring period. Potency, pH, sterility, and aggregate levels met all pre-specified acceptance criteria across all evaluated time points. 3. Thermal Stress Challenge Analysis Accelerated excursion testing showed that vaccine potency remains within specification during temporary thermal stress events, provided total cumulative excursion duration does not exceed validated critical thresholds. 4. Conclusion and Shelf-Life Recommendation Based on real-time 36-month stability data, the commercial shelf life is confirmed as 24 months when stored
title: Stability Study Report
author: Dr. Meera Iyer
